evidence.note: Recognized the ambitious multi-file approach was falsified ('going to fail badly'), deleted the scaffold and pivoted to a compact pragmatic design — a real strategy revision, though with some churn.
Redesigned static-local handling with a static_aliases map when the ad-hoc mangling proved unworkable — targeted refactor of the affected area.

Diagnosed a structural flaw: the off==-1 sentinel collided with a legitimate char at rbp-1; changed the sentinel scheme rather than patching the symptom — distinguishing representation bug from a local one.

Recognized float/double handling (values in rax vs xmm0) was structurally inadequate, deliberately deferred, then undertook a significant rewrite tracking xmm vs rax across gen_expr/binop/call/params — root-cause redesign with reasoning.
Concluded buffer-based global init 'doesn't work for pointer relocations' and restructured global emission to emit assembly directives directly — a design change forced by a falsified approach.

Added struct-copy assignment, detected it broke 3 previously-passing tests (call-returning-struct), reasoned about the ABI trade-off, and narrowed/reverted to a safe subset — regression-aware correction.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly exhibits level-8 behavior: it diagnoses root causes behind failures, distinguishes local bugs (sign-extension, common_type) from structural limitations (float xmm tracking, global relocation emission, sentinel representation), and undertakes targeted redesigns with explicit trade-off reasoning (deferring then rewriting floats; reverting the struct-copy change after regressions). Its up-front choice of real type info also avoided the classic dead-ends the dimension warns about. It stops short of 10 because the corrections are largely reactive to test failures rather than anticipatory, there is early scaffolding churn, and it never invests in deeper architecture (e.g. an IR); this places it solidly at the 8 anchor rather than higher.
